sourceEvidence.claim: Row 1 — Growth signal self-sufficiency: mutations in genes encoding proto-oncogenes (↑ growth factors → autocrine loop, ↑ PDGF in brain tumors), growth factor receptors (constitutive signaling, HER2 in breast cancer), signaling molecules (RAS), transcription factors (MYC), cell cycle regulators (cyclins, CDKs)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Growth signal
self-sufficiency

Mutations in genes encoding:
▘ Proto-oncogenes → ↑ growth factors → autocrine loop (eg, ↑ PDGF in brain tumors)
▘ Growth factor receptors → constitutive signaling (eg, HER2 in breast cancer)
▘ Signaling molecules (eg, RAS)
▘ Transcription factors (eg, MYC)
▘ Cell cycle regulators (eg, cyclins, CDKs)
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Row 5 — Sustained angiogenesis: ↑ pro-angiogenic factors (eg, VEGF) or ↓ inhibitory factors; tumor or stromal production; sprouting neoangiogenesis vs bone-marrow-recruited vasculogenesis; leaky and/or dilated vessels
sourceEvidence.quote:
Sustained
angiogenesis

↑ pro-angiogenic factors (eg, VEGF) or ↓ inhibitory factors. Factors may be produced by tumor or
stromal cells. Vessels can sprout from existing capillaries (neoangiogenesis) or endothelial cells are
recruited from bone marrow (vasculogenesis). Vessels may be leaky and/or dilated.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Row 6 — Warburg effect: shift of glucose metabolism from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis even under aerobic conditions; driven by pyruvate kinase M2 and LDH-A; supplies biosynthetic intermediates for nucleotide, lipid, and amino acid synthesis; ↑ lactate production
sourceEvidence.quote:
Warburg effect

Shift of glucose metabolism from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, even under
aerobic conditions. Driven by altered metabolic enzymes (eg, pyruvate kinase M2, LDH-A).
Aerobic glycolysis supplies rapidly dividing cancer cells with biosynthetic intermediates for
nucleotide, lipid, and amino acid synthesis, resulting in ↑ lactate production.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Row 7 — Immune evasion in cancer: ↓ MHC class I expression → cytotoxic T cells unable to recognize tumor cells; immunosuppressive factors (eg, TGF-β) + regulatory T cell recruitment; immune checkpoint upregulation
sourceEvidence.quote:
Immune evasion in
cancer

Normally, immune cells can recognize and attack tumor cells. For successful tumorigenesis, tumor
cells must evade the immune system. Multiple escape mechanisms exist:
▘ ↓ MHC class I expression by tumor cells → cytotoxic T cells are unable to recognize tumor
cells.
▘ Tumor cells secrete immunosuppressive factors (eg, TGF-β) and recruit regulatory T cells to
downregulate immune response.
▘ Tumor cells upregulate immune checkpoint molecules, which inhibit immune response.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Row 8 — Tissue invasion: E-cadherin loss → loosening of intercellular junctions → metalloproteinases degrade basement membrane and ECM → attach to laminin/fibronectin → locomotion → vascular dissemination
sourceEvidence.quote:
Tissue invasion

Loss of E-cadherin function → loosening of intercellular junctions → metalloproteinases degrade
basement membrane and ECM → cells attach to ECM proteins (eg, laminin, fibronectin) → cells
migrate through degraded ECM (“locomotion”) → vascular dissemination.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Row 9 — Metastasis: tumor cells or emboli spread via lymphatics or blood → adhesion to endothelium → extravasation and homing; site predicted by the first-encountered capillary bed; organ tropism (lung cancers commonly metastasize to adrenals)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Metastasis

Tumor cells or emboli spread via lymphatics or blood → adhesion to endothelium → extravasation
and homing. Site of metastasis can be predicted by site of 1° tumor, as the target organ is often the
first-encountered capillary bed. Some cancers show organ tropism (eg, lung cancers commonly
metastasize to adrenals).

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the nine-row table only; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The six-band reading protocol (GROWTH AXIS / DEATH AXIS / IMMORTALITY / SUPPLY LINES / IMMUNE ESCAPE / SPREAD) and the gas-pedal/brake-line framing of rows 1–2 — KYP's synthesis of the nine rows into one map.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the rows as an unstructured list; the banding, the two-axes framing, and the station numbering are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + the registry visual's band structure + pivots

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (GROW, IGNORE, REFUSE DEATH, NEVER AGE, FEED, FERMENT, HIDE, INVADE, SPREAD / GAS ON, BRAKES CUT / GLUCOSE IN, LACTATE OUT, OXYGEN IGNORED / UNGLUE, CHEW, GRAB, CRAWL, EMBARK, LAND) — no mnemonic prints on the page.
kypExtensions.rationale: No mnemonic prints anywhere on book 217 (VLM census confirmed); the four codes are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + the visual's station footers + the steps block

kypExtensions.summary: The assay-matching miniCase (telomerase positivity + glucose-to-lactate conversion under normal oxygen tension + the adrenal-nodule distractor) — a KYP-authored integration of rows 4, 6, and 9.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the rows separately and never asks the learner to match laboratory findings to hallmark pairs; the vignette, the four distractors, and the half-right near-miss option are KYP's design.
